transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Acme Head of ML), Ravi Singh (Eng Manager), Tom Elliott (Product), Maria Lopez (Procurement)

[00:00] Alice Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. This is our final weekly sync in the pilot cadence, so the goal today is to go over the results, the tuning we did last week, and make sure we're aligned on the success criteria and next steps for closeout.
[00:12] Jenna Park: Thanks Alice. Yep, excited to see the numbers. We pulled some additional logs this morning after Marcus's patch.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: cool, sorry slight echo on my end. I pushed the batching tweak and turned on the prefix kv cache - I think the transcript earlier said K V cash - lol - but it's the K-V cache.
[00:34] Ravi Singh: Right, and we also validated the quantized model variant on a subset of requests; latency looked promising.
[00:42] Tom Elliott: quick ask before we dive, can we get a one-line on whether hosted would have cut it vs dedicated? we told execs both options.
[00:51] Alice Chen: short answer: hosted is easiest to start but dedicated gives predictable tail latency at scale and better unit cost for high throughput. We'll show the numbers.
[01:03] Marcus Lee: jumping in with the numbers: overall token-level latency p50 improved from 180ms to 120ms after batching and cache; p95 dropped from 520ms to 260ms on the test set. Cost per 1k tokens with quantization is down roughly 42% on dedicated runs vs hosted baseline, but that depends on your concurrency profile.
[01:30] Jenna Park: that's good. On our side, for checkout-related prompts the precision of slot extraction is at 92% which meets our product team threshold, but for some long-form returns the hallucination rate is still higher than we'd like.
[01:47] Marcus Lee: understood. For hallucinations we recommended prompt templates + stronger system messages and a small reranker. We tested a lightweight reranker and saw false positive reductions ~20%.
[02:05] Ravi Singh: can you remind us which model variant you used for the reranker? the naming got a bit fuzzy in the notes.
[02:12] Marcus Lee: sure — it's the redwood-v2-midline-quant (note: in the transcript and deck there was a typo 'redwood v two midline'). The reranker runs on a smaller encoder-only model which is cheap.
[02:25] Tom Elliott: on security, Maria had some outstanding questions about key management and audit logs.
[02:31] Maria Lopez: yeah, specifically: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS in the private deployment, and are all inference logs stored encrypted at rest with retention control?
[02:40] Alice Chen: yes to both. For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; logs are encrypted and you can configure retention in the console. We'll share the security pack that includes SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[02:53] Maria Lopez: and SSO/SAML? we need RBAC tied to our directory.
[02:57] Alice Chen: SSO/SAML supported, with role mappings and audit log export. We'll include a short implementation checklist.
[03:07] Jenna Park: back to results — Marcus, you mentioned the dedicated benchmark. can you summarize the differences between your dedicated test and our hosted runs?
[03:17] Marcus Lee: yep. Dedicated runs used 4x A100-equivalent GPUs on a pinned pool, with autoscale off and a fixed batching window to simulate your concurrency. That reduces jitter and gives us predictable p95. Hosted baseline was on mixed fleet with autoscale and had slightly higher p95 variance. Also, caching mechanisms are more effective when you control the instance lifecycle.
[03:40] Ravi Singh: are there any functional differences we'd see in behavior? or just performance and cost?
[03:45] Marcus Lee: purely infra/behavioral — models and logits are the same. But quantization artifacts can slightly change tokenization edge cases; we flagged two prompts where quantized outputs trimmed punctuation. We recommended a short post-process normalization.
[04:03] Tom Elliott: let's talk success criteria — Jenna, you had a doc with thresholds. can we pull that up?
[04:10] Jenna Park: yes. main criteria from product: 1) extraction precision >= 90% on checkout intents (we're at 92%); 2) p95 latency <= 300ms for common paths (we're at ~260ms on dedicated tests); 3) cost per 1k tokens under $2.50 on your expected traffic (our calc was about $2.10 with dedicated and quantization); 4) security/compliance checks passed by security (open).
[04:40] Alice Chen: sounds like you're hitting product thresholds already. The outstanding items are security signoff and procurement timeline. On security signoff, Marcus will send the detailed logs and we will provide the SOC2 pack.
[04:52] Marcus Lee: I will also attach the raw benchmark CSVs so you can run independent analysis. There may be some noisy samples at tails due to a few long-context cases.
[05:05] Maria Lopez: procurement: our cycle is typically 3 weeks for a pilot to a PO, but if legal flags any terms it can push. we'll need the SOW and pricing by mid next week.
[05:16] Alice Chen: we can get that to you. I'll draft an SOW with two options: hosted monthly usage and a dedicated 3-month reserved pool with an option to convert to annual.
[05:27] Tom Elliott: pricing question: if we start hosted and then move to dedicated, are there migration fees or downtime?
[05:34] Alice Chen: no migration fees; we support one-click model pin and routing changes. There is a short warm-up for caches, but we have migration runbooks. We'll include migration steps in the SOW.
[05:46] Jenna Park: for the final exec review, can we have a 10-minute slide on cost and a 5-minute demo of the improved extraction?
[05:54] Alice Chen: absolutely. Marcus — can you prep a 5-minute demo clip and metrics slide?
[06:00] Marcus Lee: yep. I'll prepare a short recording and the metrics slide.
[06:05] Ravi Singh: on the technical side, one ask: can Redwood provide trace-level latency breakdowns per token for our biggest flows? We want to see network vs compute vs batching time.
[06:14] Marcus Lee: we can. I'll share the trace exports — they include per-token timings and the batching queue times. Be aware there's a small sampling overhead.
[06:23] Maria Lopez: another procurement concern: do you offer standard mutual NDA or do we need a redlined contract?
[06:28] Alice Chen: we have a standard pilot SOW and NDA. If you redline we'll review; typical turnaround is a few days.
[06:34] Tom Elliott: any blockers from Redwood's side to go live on dedicated if we sign?
[06:40] Marcus Lee: from infra, no blockers. We'll provision a VPC peering or private link, set up KMS, and schedule a brief cutover test. Lead time for hardware pools is currently ~7 business days; we'll confirm at contract time.
[06:57] Jenna Park: what's the expected improvement in cost if we commit annual vs the 3-month reserved?
[07:04] Alice Chen: ballpark another 10-20% off unit costs for annual reserved commitment; we'll put concrete tiers in the SOW.
[07:12] Ravi Singh: one technical nuance — when we tested the quantized path we saw slight output differences on long sequences. can we get a quick test harness to validate regressions before we flip traffic?
[07:22] Marcus Lee: yes, we'll provide a small test harness and the eval harness we used; you can run on your sample corpus. It includes diffing tools and token-level scoring.
[07:33] Tom Elliott: great. on the commercial timeline, Maria, if we get SOW by 8/19, is week of 8/26 realistic for exec sign-off?
[07:40] Maria Lopez: probably yes, but legal could push. I'll aim to have PO ready that week; worst case 2 weeks after SOW if redlines happen.
[07:50] Alice Chen: ok let's recap and assign next steps.
[07:54] Alice Chen: Recap: Redwood sends SOW + pricing (Alice), SE shares raw dedicated benchmark logs and demo clip (Marcus), Customer provides final success criteria spreadsheet and sample workload (Jenna), Procurement provides PO timeline (Maria).
[08:10] Jenna Park: quick question: are we expected to sign anything special for dedicated access related to data residency?
[08:16] Alice Chen: if you're using Private deployment or VPC, we can accommodate region pinning and residency controls. We'll include options.
[08:24] Ravi Singh: nicetohave: can we have an option for a short SLA for pilot window? even if it's not full enterprise SLA.
[08:31] Alice Chen: we can include a pilot SLA with basic uptime targets in the SOW.
[08:36] Tom Elliott: any further open technical issues?
[08:39] Marcus Lee: just two small items: the quantize edge-case fixes and the post-process normalizer I mentioned. I'll include test cases.
[08:47] Jenna Park: alright. sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:50] Alice Chen: thanks everyone — closing notes: we'll follow up with the docs and SOW. Expect the SOW and pricing by 2025-08-19; Marcus will send logs by 2025-08-15. If there's no other business we'll adjourn.
[08:59] Maria Lopez: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard product names and typos (e.g., 'K V cash' for K-V cache; 'redwood v two' instead of 'redwood-v2'). References to attachments: internal benchmark CSVs, security pack link (to be shared), SOW draft (to be shared).
